skills.trigger: When evaluating axial CT images for recurrence of an extrapulmonary pleural tumor (e.g., hemangiopericytoma) and needing to distinguish the specific location and morphology of the mass from other intrathoracic pathologies.
steps: Scan the axial CT slices specifically at the level of the diaphragm and posterior costophrenic sulcus to identify any soft tissue density distinct from the lung parenchyma.
Assess the margins of any identified mass; look for a well-defined, lobulated contour which is characteristic of this tumor type, rather than irregular or spiculated edges.

Distinguish the finding from alternatives by confirming the mass is epidiaphragmatic and pleural-based (adjacent to chest wall/diaphragm) rather than located in the upper lung fields, appearing as multiple subpleural nodules, or manifesting primarily as osteolytic rib destruction.
